note: Wire table image-read at 300 dpi from book5-6.pdf PDF p.31 (Phase 5 Step 6, 2026-10-13): all 47 lines match wiresPrinted; ER-35 is prose only, so wires = as_printed and errata_applied is empty. Script follows the printed procedure twice. Run 1: power on, push pushbutton 6, lights 1 through 6 come on in order, then push pushbutton 5 when light 6 has come on. Then the ER-35 re-set (errata.pdf PDF p.3, 'page 25: Note — to re-set the automatic sequence control, turn power OFF, then ON again.'): power off, power on. Run 2: push pushbutton 6 again, and push pushbutton 5 as soon as light 3 has come on, to exercise 'the sequence can be stopped at any time'. Asserted, printed text only: each light comes on (until), and 'in order' as every later light still off at the moment each light comes on; after the run-2 stop, lights 4, 5 and 6 still off after a 10 s window. Not asserted: 'pushing pushbutton 5 will turn the system off' names no observable (in this simulator lights 2-6 stay lit, relays 1-5 holding through their own N.O. contacts; ER-35's power OFF/ON re-set note is consistent with that), so the run-1 pushbutton 5 press carries no expect; the re-set's resulting state is not printed; timing against dial position, whether earlier lights stay on, and the motor stopping are not printed (Step 7). Run 1's start dial position c0 is the construction state, not printed: the page sets no rotary position. Run 2 starts where run 1's stop left the dial (the c11-c12 gap, after the drive-removed coast offset, 9.54 deg since 2026-10-14; c12 at the earlier invented 20 deg). Run 2's asserts hold for any run-1 rest position except D15, where the wiper (D16/M+) feeds 5C/D15 at power-on and light 2 lights before pushbutton 6 is pushed. Run 2's own stop leaves the dial in the c14-c15 gap at 9.54 deg (on D15 at the earlier 20 deg). From that gap the wiper touches no pad at power-on, so this script no longer leads to the D15 case; from D15 a further ER-35 re-set would not clear light 2 (O-C10). Both are derived and not asserted (Step 7). Rotary geometry, run rate, coast and fitted motor resistances remain profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3 and O-R5.
